spec.title: Fix canBorrow authorization guard
spec.problem: src/auth/borrower.mjs currently exports `canBorrow = user => !!user`, a truthiness check that grants borrowing rights to any truthy value, including arrays, plain objects with no role, and users with non-borrower roles (e.g. bookseller, admin) or invalid ids (zero, negative, fractional, string, NaN, Infinity, or beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). This is an authorization bypass: it does not enforce the intended rule that only a user object with role exactly 'borrower' and a positive safe-integer id may borrow. The fixed oracle test/acceptance.mjs fully specifies the required behavior and must remain unchanged.
scope: Rewrite canBorrow(user) in src/auth/borrower.mjs as a pure, deny-by-default predicate: return true only when user is a non-null, non-array object with user.role === 'borrower' (exact string match) and Number.isSafeInteger(user.id) && user.id > 0.
Reject null, undefined, arrays, primitives (including strings), and plain objects missing or mismatching role/id, returning false for all of them.
Reject non-borrower roles (e.g. bookseller, admin) even when id is otherwise valid.
Reject invalid ids: 0, negative, fractional, string-typed, NaN, Infinity, and values exceeding Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, even when role is 'borrower'.
Do not mutate the input object; the function must accept a frozen (Object.freeze) valid user and still return true.

Optionally add supplementary regression tests in test/regression.mjs covering additional negative/adversarial cases beyond the fixed oracle (e.g. negative ids, extra unexpected fields, role as array/object) without altering test/acceptance.mjs.
outOfScope: Implementing login, sessions, or any authentication scheme.
Adding a database, persistence layer, or role-permission mapping abstraction.
Modifying test/acceptance.mjs (must remain unchanged as the fixed oracle).
Adding dependencies, lockfiles, or infrastructure/config changes.
Coercing or normalizing id/role values (e.g. accepting numeric strings or case-insensitive role matching).
Generalizing to support future roles beyond borrower/bookseller/admin.

acceptance.description: canBorrow returns true for a plain object {id:1, role:'borrower'} and for an equivalent frozen (Object.freeze) object, and the input is not mutated.
acceptance.verification: node --test executes test/acceptance.mjs assertions for {id:1,role:'borrower'} and the frozen {id:2,role:'borrower'} case; both equal true.

acceptance.verification: node --test executes test/acceptance.mjs loop over [null,undefined,[],{},'borrower',...]; all equal false.

acceptance.verification: node --test executes test/acceptance.mjs cases {id:1,role:'bookseller'} and {id:1,role:'admin'}; both equal false.

acceptance.verification: Code review of src/auth/borrower.mjs confirms no assignment to user or user.* properties and no I/O; the frozen-object case in AC1 would throw under strict mutation, so its passing further confirms purity.

decisions.question: Should canBorrow reject any input shape not covered by the fixed acceptance oracle (deny-by-default), or only the specific negative cases enumerated in the oracle?
decisions.answer: Deny-by-default: canBorrow must return true only for the narrow valid shape (non-null, non-array object with role==='borrower' exactly and Number.isSafeInteger(id) && id>0) and false for every other input, not merely the cases explicitly enumerated in test/acceptance.mjs. The oracle's cases are representative, not exhaustive.

tasks.title: Rewrite canBorrow as a pure deny-by-default guard
tasks.description: In src/auth/borrower.mjs, replace `export const canBorrow = user => !!user;` with a pure predicate that returns true only when: user is a non-null object, Array.isArray(user) is false, user.role === 'borrower' (strict string equality, no coercion or case-folding), and Number.isSafeInteger(user.id) is true and user.id > 0. All other inputs (null, undefined, arrays, primitives including strings, plain objects with missing/wrong-typed role or id, non-borrower roles, id of 0/negative/fractional/string/NaN/Infinity/beyond MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) must return false. Do not assign to or otherwise mutate `user` or any of its properties, so that a frozen input still works and returns true when valid. Keep the function pure: no I/O, no logging, no new imports or dependencies. Reuse the existing exported symbol name `canBorrow` (src/auth/borrower.mjs:1) so test/acceptance.mjs's import continues to resolve. Optionally add test/regression.mjs with `node --test` style assertions (import from '../src/auth/borrower.mjs') covering supplementary adversarial cases (e.g. negative id, role as an array/object, extra unexpected fields on an otherwise valid user) — these are additive only and must not alter or duplicate the behavior asserted by the unmodified test/acceptance.mjs.

experience.rationale: canBorrow is a pure backend authorization predicate with no UI surface; no frontend, route, or visual change is involved.

threatModel.summary: canBorrow(user) is a deny-by-default authorization predicate consumed by an unspecified caller to decide whether to grant a library loan. The function itself has no persistence, network, or session boundary; the trust boundary is the argument passed in by its caller, which may originate from untrusted request data upstream. The current implementation (`!!user`) collapses this boundary to a mere truthiness check, allowing elevation of privilege (any truthy value, including a bookseller or malformed object, is treated as an authorized borrower) and type confusion (arrays, strings, and objects with invalid ids pass). The fix restores deny-by-default behavior: only an exact role match and a validated positive safe-integer id authorize the action; every other shape is denied, and the function never logs, persists, or discloses the input, so no separate logging/audit mechanism is introduced or required.
assets: Library loan authorization decision (the boolean returned by canBorrow)
User role and id fields passed into the predicate
trustBoundaries: Boundary between canBorrow's caller (which supplies the user object, potentially derived from untrusted request/session data) and the predicate itself — canBorrow must not trust shape, type, or presence of any field.

threats.description: A caller passes an object with a non-borrower role (e.g. bookseller or admin) or a malformed/truthy non-object value; the current `!!user` check incorrectly authorizes it, letting a non-borrower or malformed principal borrow.
mitigations: Require user to be a non-null, non-array object
Require user.role === 'borrower' via strict equality, no coercion or case-insensitive matching

threats.description: A caller supplies an id that is not a genuine positive integer (0, negative, fractional, numeric string, NaN, Infinity, or a value exceeding Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), which could bypass downstream integer-based lookups or cause unexpected coercion/overflow behavior if authorized.
mitigations: Require Number.isSafeInteger(user.id) && user.id > 0 with no coercion of string-typed ids

threats.description: An authorization check that mutates its input could corrupt caller-held state or bypass immutability guarantees (e.g. a frozen user record), creating inconsistent authorization state across calls.
mitigations: Implement canBorrow as side-effect-free: read-only property access, no assignment to user or its properties, verified by accepting a frozen valid object and still returning true

assumptions: The caller of canBorrow is responsible for authenticating the principal and constructing the user object; canBorrow only validates the shape and authorization of the object it is given.
No logging or audit trail is required inside canBorrow itself; it is a pure predicate and introduces no disclosure risk since it neither logs nor persists its input.

requirements.title: Deny-by-default role and id authorization check
requirements.verification: node --test runs test/acceptance.mjs, which exercises the full positive and negative matrix (valid borrower, frozen valid borrower, null/undefined/array/empty-object/string, non-borrower roles, and every invalid id case); all assertions pass.
negativeTests: plain object with no role or id

requirements.title: No side effects or state disclosure from the authorization predicate
requirements.verification: Code review confirms canBorrow performs only read access to its argument and returns a boolean with no I/O, logging, or mutation; the frozen-object test case in test/acceptance.mjs would throw under strict mode if mutation were attempted, so its pass further verifies purity.
negativeTests: Passing a frozen valid user object must not throw and must return true, proving no attempted mutation

assumptions: test/acceptance.mjs is the complete and authoritative behavioral contract for canBorrow and will not be edited by the implementation task.
No authentication, session, or persistence layer is being introduced; canBorrow remains a standalone pure predicate.
deferred: Generalizing to a role-permission map for additional roles or capabilities beyond borrow/deny is out of scope until a future request requires more than a binary borrower check.

architecture.summary: Architecture decision for fixing canBorrow(user): replace the current `!!user` truthiness check with a pure, deny-by-default guard-clause predicate enforcing role === 'borrower' (exact match) and Number.isSafeInteger(id) with id > 0, rejecting null/arrays/malformed objects and never mutating input. This directly satisfies every case in the fixed test/acceptance.mjs oracle, which fully specifies the contract (positive/negative cases including frozen input, id 0, fractional/string/NaN/Infinity/overflow ids, and non-borrower roles). No dependencies, login, persistence, or role-permission abstraction are introduced, matching the single-file, disposable-fixture scope.

decisions.decision: Rewrite canBorrow(user) as a single pure, deny-by-default predicate in src/auth/borrower.mjs: return true only when user is a non-null, non-array object with role === 'borrower' (exact string match, no coercion/case-folding) and Number.isSafeInteger(user.id) && user.id > 0; every other shape (null, undefined, arrays, primitives, missing/extra-typed fields, other roles, non-integer/zero/negative/NaN/Infinity/out-of-range ids) returns false. No mutation of the input, no new state, no I/O.
decisions.rationale: The acceptance oracle (test/acceptance.mjs) enumerates exactly this contract: valid borrower with positive safe-integer id passes; null/undefined/array/plain object/string, bookseller/admin roles, id 0, fractional id, string id, NaN, Infinity, and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1 must all fail; a frozen valid object must still pass, proving no mutation is attempted and none is required. A deny-by-default guard clause chain is the smallest correct structure satisfying this oracle without speculative generality.
alternatives: Use a schema/validation library (e.g. zod) for role+id shape checking
Coerce/normalize id (Number(user.id)) or role casing before comparing, to be 'lenient' with near-valid input
Generalize into a role-permission map (borrower/bookseller/admin -> capabilities) for future extensibility
tradeoffs: Hand-rolled guard clauses are slightly more verbose than a schema library call but require zero dependencies and are fully auditable for a security-sensitive predicate

Strict typeof/exact-match checks reject some 'almost valid' inputs (e.g. numeric-string ids) that a lenient coercion approach would accept; this is intentional per the deny-by-default requirement and the oracle's explicit {id:'1',role:'borrower'} negative case
A permission-map generalization would better anticipate future roles but is unrequested scope creep for a task explicitly scoped to a single boolean predicate with a fixed, frozen oracle
reconsiderWhen: A future request adds additional roles or capability tiers beyond simple borrow/deny, warranting a role-to-permission map
The id domain changes (e.g. UUIDs or string identifiers become valid), requiring the integer-based id check to be replaced
Authentication/session context becomes available and role/id must be derived from a verified principal rather than a raw object argument

inspection.finding: Current implementation is `export const canBorrow = user => !!user;` — a truthiness check that allows any truthy value (arrays, wrong roles, invalid ids), failing the authorization contract entirely.

Fixed oracle requires: {id:1,role:'borrower'} and a frozen equivalent -> true; null, undefined, [], {}, 'borrower' string, bookseller/admin roles, id 0, id 1.5, id '1' (string), id NaN, id Infinity, id MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1 -> all false. This fully specifies the exact-role-match, positive-safe-integer-id, deny-by-default contract; no other tests exist.

type: module, no dependencies, no test runner script configured — confirms this is a minimal disposable fixture; node:test/assert are used directly by the oracle, so no new dependency is needed or permitted.
